claims.evidence: Three SILAC mixtures deposited as rep1_MIX1_*, rep2_MIX2_*, rep3_MIX3-* (24 fractions each). Each mixture combined one light, one medium, one heavy lysate (PRIDE protocol "20ug from heavy, middle and light conditions were mixed"). Data S10 reports three replicates (Ratio rep1/rep2/rep3) of the conditions HepG2, HepAD38(Tet+), HepAD38(Tet-). One source = one lysate of one culture in one mixture.

claims.location: comment[label] + characteristics[cell line] + characteristics[HBV replication status] + factor values, rows 1-72 (rep1)
claims.value: rep1: SILAC light = HepG2, SILAC medium = HepAD38 Tet+, SILAC heavy = HepAD38 Tet-
claims.evidence: Data S10 sheet HepAD38(Tet-)_HepG2 "Ratio rep1" equals proteinGroups "Ratio H/L normalized 1" for 2619 of 2636 proteins (direct); sheet HepAD38(Tet-)_HepAD38(Tet+) "Ratio rep1" equals "Ratio H/M normalized 1" for 1268 of 1276. So Tet- = H, HepG2 = L, Tet+ = M. Every other column/orientation matched <=42 values (chance). Orientation: both S10 sheets share the Tet- arm, so reading each sheet name as first-named/second-named is the only reading that gives three distinct channels per replicate (reading either sheet as second/first puts Tet- on two channels or two conditions on one channel); it does so in all three replicates, giving a complete 3x3 label rotation.

limitations: No explicit sentence in the paper or PRIDE protocol states which SILAC state held which condition. The channel map comes from Supplementary Data S10 (sheet names give the condition pair, columns give per-replicate ratios) matched number-for-number against the deposited proteinGroups.txt normalized ratio columns (chanmap.out). This is a strong deterministic check, but it is a derivation, not a stated label assignment.

Mapping of file prefix repN to MaxQuant experiment N is inferred from naming (rep1/rep2/rep3 = experiments 1/2/3 = Data S10 Ratio rep1/2/3); no summary.txt/mqpar.xml/evidence.txt with a raw-file column was deposited.

rep2_MIX2_1.raw was acquired under the internal name MIX1_19_180826125008.raw (Xcalibur adds the timestamp when the name already exists). The file differs from rep1_MIX1_19.raw (153245872 vs 162930784 bytes) and its timestamp suffix says it was acquired 2018-08-26 12:50:08, in the same folder as the MIX2 runs (MIX2_5 and MIX2_12 re-acquisitions are stamped 2018-08-29). Autosampler vial positions in the raw headers (script scripts/vials.py): rep1_MIX1_19 = vial C8, rep2_MIX2_1 = vial D7, rep2_MIX2_2 = vial D8 (rep1_MIX1_1 = A6), so rep2_MIX2_1 is a different vial sitting directly before MIX2_2 in the MIX2 block; the sequence row carried a stale file name; the submitter deposited it as rep2 fraction 1, which is kept. The raw folder name 20180816_Rpn1_SILAC_RP is the instrument operator folder; the ratios match the HBV supplementary data.

comment[precursor mass tolerance] / comment[fragment mass tolerance] = not available: no mqpar.xml, parameters.txt or summary.txt deposited. parse_sdrf convert-openms therefore fails (expected, as in campaign precedents).

Variable modifications other than Oxidation (M) cannot be ruled out (e.g. MaxQuant default Acetyl (Protein N-term) leaves no site table in proteinGroups); only the evidenced ones are listed. The search also included a custom ncORF database (identifiers like R1_R6_peak_51 in proteinGroups); no HBV protein entries.
Digestion enzyme not stated anywhere; trypsin inferred from fully tryptic peptides in the deposited search.

Fractionation method of the 24 fractions per mixture is not stated (folder suffix "RP" hints at reversed-phase but is not evidence) -> not available. Alkylation reagent not stated -> not available although the search implies carbamidomethylation.

Culture medium: SILAC medium base formulation not stated (HepG2 normally DMEM; HepAD38 DMEM/F-12 for virus production) -> not available. Passage number not available. Cell type not stated (PRIDE lists hepatocyte as organism part; not used) -> not available.
Whether HepG2 cultures received tetracycline is not stated -> characteristics[treatment] not available for HepG2 rows.

The PRIDE record cites the J Hepatol 2021 paper (PMID 33621634, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2021.02.009), which is not open access and was not read; the Cell Discov 2021 paper (PMC8560872) names PXD014908 in its Data Availability and was used.
parse_sdrf validate-sdrf warnings: "tetracycline withdrawal" not an NCIT/EFO term; "15-year-old stage" is HsapDv, not EFO. Both kept deliberately (stated procedure; campaign precedent HsapDv stages).

Only 169 of 46272 peptides (0.4%) contain Cys (all carrying +57.021 Da per Cys, none unmodified). Fixed Carbamidomethyl describes the search setting; whether the samples were actually alkylated is uncertain (no alkylation step is described), so comment[alkylation reagent] stays not available.
